title: Pensacola style versus New Orleans style and band arrangement
summary: Ida says early bands played by ear, did not have the New Orleans Dixie swing, and describes instrumentation and how solos were backed.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, tell me, when you were starting out, the bands down here, did they play like Buddy Fatigue and on that R-R? Would they play strictly reading or what?

Well, the boys actually would be playing just air music, but they know how to read, some of them, because they're just young starting out, you see. But we'd go out and get gigs. We'd make good gigs money. So sometimes, you know, some could read, but mostly we'd be playing by anything we hear. We can go and play to have a good air on, you see.
Did they play like New Orleans music? No, uh-uh.
No, we didn't have that Dixie swing like New Orleans when we played our music.
It was quite a difference between New Orleans music and our music.
I've always been curious to know what the difference was.
Well, it's a lot of different. Right today, it's a lot of different in orchestration from New Orleans over here.
Who carried the melody down here?
Who carried the melody down here?
Yeah, what did I know to me?

Well, we had, just like trumpet and, let me see now, wait now, the piano, trumpet, bass, and the piano, bass, and the drum. I'm trying to say it. And they had one of them, what do you call them, homes? Sacks? No, no. Bass home. Bass home kind of thing. See, that was four, it's for the bass. And then the re-station was, there had two sacks. We had an alto, alto and that other, what, Marley Mercy blow? He blow, he played some piano. No, he played tenor. Tenor, I'm trying to say. We had first, second, you see, alto and tenor. And then trumpet. And then we have a girl to sing with, that's the way it was, baseball, and like that. We had a nice combination all night. Sure did.
And it was different from New Orleans. Sure. Who would carry the melody the most of the time when the whole band was playing?

Well, everybody, mostly I tell you, when the whole band is playing, we have it all arranged out. Whoever takes the solo, you see, well, we back them up. The whole background. Just like if Deere gonna take a solo, then trumpet solo, well, then the other party take the other solo, back him up, and a thing like that. And just like the piano player, just like I take a solo, while then the saxophone, and the horn just back me up behind the ground.
Billy? Yeah, Billy. I want you to explain the difference between New Orleans music and Pensacola music as soon as I can get a new reel on here. Okay.
